説明 [explanation]: In some situations, A in A の B is a Noun with a particle such as へ, で, と, から, and まで. が, を and に never occur in this position. Note that の cannot be omitted in this case because it indicates that the preceeding noun phrase and particle modifies the following noun phrase. Without の, the noun phrase with the particle is interpreted as an adverbial phrase modifying the predicate in the clause, i.e. compare 先生とミーチングに行けない。(I can't go to meet the teacher) and 先生とのミーチングに行けない。(I can't go to the meeting with the teacher). --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Noun + Particle + の + Noun

This particular expression, as opposed to meaning " beginning to" or "have V-ed" is the original meaning of V-te くる。 説明 [explanation]: V-teくる and V-teいく indicate the temporal or spatial direction of an action from the speaker's viewpoint. V-teくる is used when an action appears to be directed toward the speaker, and V-teいく is used when it appears to be directed away from the speaker. V-teくる often indicates that an action or process began in the past and is continuing in the present, or that something has begun to take place. V-teいく, on the other hand, often expresses an action or state that will continue from the present into the future. In other uses, 来る and 行くfollowing V-te maintain their original meanings, i.e., "to come" and "to go." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-teくる = have V-ed; begin to; become; grow V−teいく = go on V-ing; continue; become; grow --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te来る/行く

まだ 春[はる]なのに、 今日[きょう]は まるで 夏[なつ]の ように 暑[あつ]い。
It's still spring, but today is so hot it seems almost like summer.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まるで N {の／じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} ように "as if ~ (were/-ed); just like" This structure is used to introduce a simile, i.e., to describe a thing, person, action, etc. by comparing it with a similar thing, person, action, etc. まるで is an emphatic marker.
プレゼントは ５０[ごじゅう]ドル 以下[いか]の 物[もの]に しようと 思[おも]う。
I'm thinking I'll get something for $50 or less as a present.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: X以上 and X以下 means "equal to or more than X" and "(equal to or) less than X," respectively. A Number + Counter or a demonstrative pronoun such as これ and それ commonly occurs before 以上 and 以下. When the topic is academic grades, grade symbols such as C and B can be used (e.g., C以上). --- 英訳 [English translation]: 以上 = or more 以下 = less than; or less --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) 以上/以下: ３年生以上 b. Demonstrative pronoun 以上/以下: これ以上; それ以下
この 作文[さくぶん]は コンピュータを 使[つか]わずに 手[て]で 書[か]いた。
I wrote this composition by hand; I didn't use a computer.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ずに is synonymous with ないで when ないで means "without doing something" or "instead of doing something." に is sometimes omitted. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Without V-ing; instead of V-ing --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-naiずに: 行かずに; 食べずに (Exception: する->せずに
日本[にほん]に いる うちに、 色々[いろいろ]な 所[ところ]に 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]きたい。
While I'm still in Japan, I want to go visit various places.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (ない)うちに is used when someone does something before a situation or state changes. 間に is used in similar situations, but it cannot be used with the negative forms of verbs. Another difference between the two phrases is that うちに always implies that it is not possible, easy or a good idea to do something after the time specified by the うちに clause. However, this is not always the case with 間に. Thus far, if it is not a problem for the speaker to go to Japan after finishing his Japanese class, 間に should be used, as shown below: 日本語の勉強をしている間に日本に行ってみたい。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: while ~ still ～ないうちに＝ before (something happens) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ～うちに
ピアノ、 お上手[じょうず]ですね。 いつ 始[はじ]められたんですか。
You play the piano very well. May I ask when you started learning?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

る-verbs: V-masu + られる Passive forms of verbs are used to indicate politeness when the speaker refers to the actions of the hearer or someone to whom the speaker wants to show deference. However, this use of passive forms does not indicate as high a level of politeness as おV-masu になる or special honorific verbs like いらっしゃる and めし上がる。 Note that the polite form of the auxilliary verb いる is not いられる, but おられる. The auxilliary verb おられる is less polite than いらっしゃる。
エジプトは ピラミッドや スフィンクスで 有名[ゆうめい]です。
Egypt is famous for its pyramids and sphinx.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Either a noun or a sentence (S + こと) occurs before で to state what X is famous for or the reason that X is famous. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X is famous for Y; X is known because --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~は N で {有名です / 知られている} ~は S こと で {有名です / 知られている}
この 問題[もんだい]に ついて、 グループで 話[はな]し合[あ]って下[くだ]さい。
Please talk to each other in a group about this problem.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 合う, when combined with another verb, forms a compound verb, adding the meaning "to each other." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V (to/for) each other; V with~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V−masu合う: 話し合う; 見せ合う; 助け合う; 信じ合う
春[はる]だと 言[い]っても、 寒[さむ]くて まだ セーターを 着[き]ている。
It's technically spring, but it's still so cold that I'm wearing sweaters.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{ANa/N} + {だ／じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} {と／って} 言っても "although ~ say/said that ~; even though ~ say/said that ~"
この 大学[だいがく]は レベルが 高[たか]いと いう ことで 知[し]られている。
This university is known as a high-quality institution.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S-plain ということ(が、を、etc) General meaning: that; V-ing changes a sentence into a noun clause, but does not add any meaning. The noun clause can be marked by が、を, etc. This phrase is usually used in WRITTEN language.
先生[せんせい]は テニスを されるんですね。 知[し]りませんでした。
So you play tennis, Professor. I didn't know that.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

る-verbs: V-masu + られる Passive forms of verbs are used to indicate politeness when the speaker refers to the actions of the hearer or someone to whom the speaker wants to show deference. However, this use of passive forms does not indicate as high a level of politeness as おV-masu になる or special honorific verbs like いらっしゃる and めし上がる。 Note that the polite form of the auxilliary verb いる is not いられる, but おられる. The auxilliary verb おられる is less polite than いらっしゃる。
この アパートは 明[あか]るくて 広[ひろ]い。 それに、 学校[がっこう]も 近[ちか]い。
This apartment is light and spacious. On top of that, it's close to the school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: それに is used to add an item or make an addition statement. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in addition; moreover; furthermore; what's more; on top of that; and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {、/と / に} N2, それに N3 b. S1。それに、S2。 c. S1 し、それに、S2。
世界[せかい]中[じゅう]、 どこに 行[い]っても マクドナルドが 食[た]べられる。
No matter where you go throughout the world you can eat McDonald's.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ても is used with a question word, the phrase means: "no matter" or "without regard to." --- 英訳 [English translation]: no matter what/who/when/where/how --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ QW(prt)+V-teも
その 本[ほん]なら、 大学[だいがく]の 図書[としょ]館[かん]に 行[い]けば、 ある はずだよ。
That book? If you go to the university library, they should have it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A} -plain はず [seen here] ANa {な/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった) N {の/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった} "Should; I expect that ~; I believe that~" The dependent noun はず indicates that the speaker/writer or someone he/she empathizes with believes or expects that what is stated before はず is true based on his/her knowledge or memory at the moment of speech or at the time of the event stated in the main clause. The negative form can be either 〜ないはずだ or 〜はずがない.However, the sense of negation is stronger in はずがない. When Sはずだ modifies a noun, の must be used between はず and the noun.
今[いま]から 2[に], 3[さん]時間[じかん]、 図書[としょ]館[かん]に 勉強[べんきょう] しに 行[い]ってきます。
I'm off to the library to study for two or three hours.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Number1, Number2 + Counter "(2 or 3) days/times/etc.; (3,4) hours/cars/etc." Two successive numbers are used to indicate an approximate number or amount
冬[ふゆ]の 間[あいだ]、 カエルは、 まるで 死[し]んだ ように 動[うご]きません。
During the winter, frogs remain motionless as if they were dead.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まるで V-plain ように "as if ~ (were/-ed); just like" This structure is used to introduce a simile, i.e., to describe a thing, person, action, etc. by comparing it with a similar thing, person, action, etc. まるで is an emphatic marker.
私[わたし]は チョコレートが 死[し]ぬほど 好[す]きだ。 毎日[まいにち]でも 食[た]べる。
I love chocolate to death! I'd even eat it every day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
私[わたし]は あまり 人[ひと]の 意見[いけん]に 左右[さゆう] されたくないと 思[おも]っている。
I think I don't want to be swayed much by other people's opinion.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 を N2 左右する "influence; govern" 左右する is most commonly used in written language.
20[にじゅう]年[ねん]も 乗[の]っていた 車[くるま]が ついに 動[うご]かなくなってしまった。
The car we used for as many as 20 years finally stopped working.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The adverb ついに indicates that something happens or something expected doesn't happen, after waiting for it, longing for it, expecting it to happen, making an effort to make it happen, or after struggling/suffering in a hard situation for a long time. --- 英訳 [English translation]: at last; finally; in the end; after all --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ついに
いったい あなたは 何[なに]を 考[かんが]えて そんな ことを したんですか。
What in the world were you thinking, doing something like that?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

いったい QW "(what, who, where, how, etc.) on earth" いったい is an intensifier used with questions. It usually occurs immediately preceding the question word, but it may appear in other locations before the QW, as seen here.
台風[たいふう]が 近[ちか]づいてきたので、 風[かぜ]が ますます 強[つよ]くなってきた。
Because a typhoon drew near, the wind grew stronger and stronger.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ますます A-stem くなる increasingly; even more; even -er; still more; still -er" ますます occurs with verbs, the adverbial forms of adjectives and adverbs. It indicates that something happens to an even greater (or lesser) degree than before. ますます is NOT used for future controllable events. For example, it cannot replace もっともっと in もっともっとがんばって下さい。
その ロボットは 人間[にんげん]と 同[おな]じぐらい 上手[じょうず]に 自転[じてん]車[しゃ]に 乗[の]れる。
That robot can ride a bike about as well as a human can.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The particle ぐらい/くらい "approximately" often occurs with 同じ to mean "about the same." --- 英訳 [English translation]: about as ~ as; about the same ~ as ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N と同じ{ぐらい/くらい} b. N1 と同じ{ぐらい/くらい}の N2
この アパートは 広[ひろ]いから、 二人[ふたり]で 住[す]めるんじゃないかな。
This apartment's big enough that two people could probably live in it, I think...
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This ending indicates the speaker's conjecture and is used to express an opinion in an indecisive fashion. Although the negative form ではない is used, there is no negative meaning. のではない{だろう/でしょう}か are used only in written language, and のではないだろうか is the more formal form. ん{ではないでしょうか/じゃないかな} are used only in spoken language. んじゃないかな is more casual. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I think that ~; Isn't it that~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Sのではないでしょうか。
作文[さくぶん]を 書[か]く 時[とき]は、 なるべく 漢字[かんじ]を 使[つか]う ようにして下[くだ]さい。
Do your best to use as many kanji as possible when writing your essays.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: なるべく with or without an adverb modifies the following verb phrase and adds the meaning "as (much) as possible." When there is no specific adverb after なるべく, it is usually interpreted as "as much as~" or "as often as~." --- 英訳 [English translation]: as much/often as possible; as ~ as possible --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ なるべく
チェックは 使[つか]えませんが、 クレジット カードなら 使[つか]えます。
You can't use a check, but you can use a credit card.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: なら is used when the speaker supposes that something is the case or is true and makes a statement, suggestion, etc. based on that supposition. の occurs before なら when the supposition is based on what the speaker has heard from someone or learned from the situation. Nなら means "if it is N; N would/could ~." In "S1 なら S2", the action/event in S1 does not have to take place before that in S2. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Nなら = would; could~ S(の)なら = if (it's the case that) ~; if (it's true that) ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~(の)なら
夏休[なつやす]みは イタリヤや ギリシャなどに 行[い]こうと 思[おも]っています。
I'm thinking of going to Italy and Greece (and other places around there) over summer vacation.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: など indicates that the given list is not exhaustive. When more than one item is listed, や is commonly used to connect the item. --- 英訳 [English translation]: N1やN2など = N1, N2 and others. N1やN2などのN3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. N1やN2など、N3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N1やN2など({は / も / が / を / に / の / etc.)} (N1 and N2 can be words or phrases).
この ロボットは、 まるで 人間[にんげん]の ように 歩[ある]く ことが できます。
This robot can walk just like a human.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まるで N {の／じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} ように "as if ~ (were/-ed); just like" This structure is used to introduce a simile, i.e., to describe a thing, person, action, etc. by comparing it with a similar thing, person, action, etc. まるで is an emphatic marker.
私[わたし]は、 何[なん]年[ねん]か 前[まえ]、 ニューヨークである 有名[ゆうめい]人[じん]に 会[あ]いました。
A few years ago, I met a celebrity in New York.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: あるN is used when the speaker has a specific X in mind but does not want/need to be specific. ある日 refers to a specific day, ある有名人 refers to (a) specific famous person/people and ある所 refers to an imaginary place in a folk tale. --- 英訳 [English translation]: a; a certain; some; some (one/thing) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ あるN: ある人; ある町; ある年
映画[えいが]が 好[す]きなので、 毎週[まいしゅう]の ように 映画[えいが]を 見[み]に 行[い]っています。
I like movies, so I go to see a movie almost every week.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The literal meaning of this phrase is "like every ~," but it is used to mean "almost every ~." --- 英訳 [English translation]: almost every ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 毎Xのように (X = time word): 毎{日/週/月/年/回}のように
母[はは]が 教[おし]えてくれた 通[とお]り 作[つく]ったら、 おいしい ケーキが できた。
I made it just as my mother taught me, and the cake turned out great.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 通り（に） "the way; as; exactly like; following; according to" When 通り is modified by a verb or noun, it means "the way; as someone does; as something indicates." 通り can also be used as a suffix, in which case 通り is directly affixed to nouns and the pronunciation changes from とおり to どおり。
母[はは]が 病気[びょうき]なので、 休[やす]みの たびに 家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]る ようにしています。
My mother's sick, so every time we have a break I try to go home.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Nのたびに "every time; each time; on every ~; whenever" たびに expresses the idea that each time someone does something, something else takes place. When たびに is modified by a noun, the noun refers to an action or certain time.
四国[しこく]は とても いい 所[ところ]だったから、 また 行[い]きたいと 思[おも]います。
Shikoku was really nice, so I think I'd like to go there again.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: In addition to the meaning "again," また expresses the meaning "also" or "additionally." --- 英訳 [English translation]: also; as well; additionally; in addition; moreover --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ また、S。
会社[かいしゃ]への 行[い]きがけに 銀行[ぎんこう]に よって、 お金[かね]を おろして行[い]こう。
Let's stop at the bank on the way to work and withdraw some money.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-masu がけに "on one's way" がけに is used with the masu-stem of motion verbs like 行く、来る、and 帰る to mean "on one's way."
「話[はな]せる」と いうのは、 「話[はな]す ことが できる」と いう 意味[いみ]だ。
Hanaseru means "to be able to speak".
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The structure ~というのは~だ is used to provide the meaning or definition of a word or phrase. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X means ~; The meaning of X is ~; What X means is ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. ~ というのは {Nのこと / N ということ}だ b. ~ というのは Sことだ. Type 2c c. ~ というのは {Sということ/Sという意味}だ. Type 1
日本[にほん]語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] してみたいと 思[おも]う。 一方[いっぽう]、 フランス語[ご]も いいね。
I think I would like to try learning Japanese. On the other hand, French is nice too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1. 一方(で) 、S2. [S1 could be a VN] "On the other hand," The conjunction 一方 is used to present two contrastive situations or two concurrent states, events or actions. 一方 is usually used in written language.
ほら、 これ、 見[み]て。 リリーが 子犬[こいぬ]の 時[とき]の 写真[しゃしん]。 かわいいねえ。
Here, take a look at this. It's a picture of Lily when she was a puppy. Isn't she cute?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほら "Look!; See?; Come on!" The interjection ほら can be used to draw the hearer's attention to something. Only used in very casual conversation.
私[わたし]は テニスを する ことは しますが、 あまり 上手[じょうず]じゃありません。
I do play tennis, but I'm not very good at it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A} - plain.aff ことは {V/A}-plain.aff (が／けれど） "It is certainly true that~, but; indeed ~, but; do V ~, but; ~ is/are/was/etc. ~, but" This structure is used when the speaker/writer admits that the proposition is true but wants to qualify the proposition with an additional remark.
日本[にほん]中[じゅう]を 安[やす]く 旅行[りょこう] する ために、 JR パスを 買[か]おうと 思[おも]っている。
I'm thinking of buying a JR pass so that I can travel around Japan cheaply.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by a noun or the non-past form of a verb, it indicates either purpose or reason/cause. In different contexts, Noun のため(に) also indicates benefit. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in order to; to; for the purpose of; for; for the sake of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nのため(に) N1のためのN2 Verb plainため(に) Verb plainためのN
この サイトに アクセス すると、 毎回[まいかい]の ように フリーズ してしまう。
My computer freezes almost every time I access this website.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The literal meaning of this phrase is "like every ~," but it is used to mean "almost every ~." --- 英訳 [English translation]: almost every ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 毎Xのように (X = time word): 毎{日/週/月/年/回}のように
あの 人[ひと]には 5[ご]， 6[ろく]回[かい] あった ことが あるが、 話[はな]した ことは 一度[いちど]も ない。
I've met that person five or six times, but we haven't talked even once.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Number1, Number2 + Counter "(2 or 3) days/times/etc.; (3,4) hours/cars/etc." Two successive numbers are used to indicate an approximate number or amount
1[いち]日[にち]中[ちゅう] コンピュータを 使[つか]っている せいで、 目[め]が 悪[わる]くなってしまった。
Because I use a computer all day long, my eyesight has gotten worse.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain せい "because; due to" Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result.
日本[にほん]語[ご]の クラスの 外[そと]でも、 なるべく 日本[にほん]語[ご]で 話[はな]した 方[ほう]が いいですよ。
Even when outside Japanese class, it is best to speak in Japanese as often as possible.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: なるべく with or without an adverb modifies the following verb phrase and adds the meaning "as (much) as possible." When there is no specific adverb after なるべく, it is usually interpreted as "as much as~" or "as often as~." --- 英訳 [English translation]: as much/often as possible; as ~ as possible --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ なるべく
日本[にほん]語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] している 外国[がいこく]人[じん]は 多[おお]くなってきていると 言[い]えるだろう。
It'd probably be safe to say that the number of foreigners studying Japanese has been increasing.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This pattern is used when the speaker is quite certain that his/her statement is correct but wants to soften the statement so as not to appear too assertive. This is a formal expression. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It probably can be said that ~; it is probably all right to say that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S-plain と言えるだろう
トムは 明日[あした] 試験[しけん]が ある。だから 今日[きょう]の パーティーには 来[こ]ないと 思[おも]う。
Tom has a test tomorrow. That's why I don't think he'll come to today's party.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: It is a sentence-initial conjunction. It precedes a fact, conclusion, decision, etc. S1 is the cause/reason for the information stated in S2. それで cannot be used when S2 is the speaker's judgement, request or command. In this situation, だから should be used, as shown in this example sentence. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because of that; so; that's why; for that reason --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S１。それで、S２。
この 地方[ちほう]は 北[きた]に あるので、 夏[なつ]は 午前[ごぜん] 4[よ]時[じ] 前[まえ]に 空[そら]が 明[あか]るくなってくる。
Because this area is in the north, in the summer it starts to get light here before 4:00 am.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-teくる and V-teいく indicate the temporal or spatial direction of an action from the speaker's viewpoint. V-teくる is used when an action appears to be directed toward the speaker, and V-teいく is used when it appears to be directed away from the speaker. V-teくる often indicates that an action or process began in the past and is continuing in the present, or that something has begun to take place. V-teいく, on the other hand, often expresses an action or state that will continue from the present into the future. In other uses, 来る and 行くfollowing V-te maintain their original meanings, i.e., "to come" and "to go." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-teくる = have V-ed; begin to; become; grow V−teいく = go on V-ing; continue; become; grow --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te来る/行く
日本[にほん]の マンガを もとに して たくさんの アニメや ゲームが 作[つく]られている。

説明 [explanation]: をもとにして is a compound particle meaning "based on."して here is optional. The noun-modification form is をもとにした. --- 英訳 [English translation]: based on --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをもとに(して) N1をもとにしたN2
私[わたし]は 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]に 話[はな]せる ことは 話[はな]せるが、 スミスさんほどでは ない。

N のほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb
レポート、 今[いま]、 書[か]いてる とこ （ろ）だから、 書[か]き終[お]わったら見[み]てくれる？

{V-plain.non-past/N} だけで {いい／十分だ／etc.} "just with ~; just by V-ing (is fine/enough/etc.) N/Vだけで is used to express the idea that X or just doing X is fine or good enough or that one can do something just with X or by doing X.

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. 少なくとも N (は） 少なくとも means "at least." It can be used with a noun or number. When used with a noun, は often follows the noun (or the particle after the noun), indicating that the noun is under focus.

~わけだ。 Means: The reason is that~; it means that~; that's why~; no wonder~; naturally Can be used in 3 situations, here it is (2) when a speaker reaches a logical conclusion based on what he/she has learned from the hearer or has discovered.

もまた "as well; also; too" In this usage もまた means the same as も; however it is more emphatic and formal than も.

説明 [explanation]: ようになる indicates a gradual change over a certain period of time; it means that someone (or something) comes to the point where he/she does (or can do) something or does not (or cannot) do something. V-なくなる is synonymous with V-ないようになる. 母[はは]と 同[おな]じで、 私[わたし]も えびの アレルギーが あるので、 えびは 食[た]べられないんです。

説明 [explanation]: The comparison phrases と同じで and と違って mean "just like ~" and "unlike ~", respectively. Note that the particle と is used when X and Y are in a reciprocal relationship --- 英訳 [English translation]: N と同じで = just like N N と違って = unlike N; different from N --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N と{同じ/違って}
車[くるま]を 止[と]めたかったら、 私[わたし]の 家[いえ]の 前[まえ]に 何[なん]台[だい]か 止[と]める ことが できますから、 どうぞ。
If you need a place to park, there's space for a few cars in front of my house, so feel free to park there.

V-plain.non-past たびに "every time; each time; on every ~; whenever" たびに expresses the idea that each time someone does something, something else takes place. When たびに is modified by a noun, the noun refers to an action or certain time.
せっかく 日本[にほん]語[ご]を ３[さん]年[ねん]も 勉強[べんきょう] したのだから、 ぜひ 一度[いちど]、 日本[にほん]に 行[い]ってみたいです。
I've spent three whole years studying Japanese, so I'd really love to visit Japan once.

せっかく V {のだから/のに} "with effort; at great pain; take the trouble to do ~; ~, which is a rare occasion/event/etc." せっかく is used in 2 situations: (1) when the speaker/writer does something with a lot of effort or at great pain ad therefore he/she wants to make use of it; or, in spite of the effort or pain, he/she cannot make use of it. (this is the case here)
この 問題[もんだい]が 分[わ]からないと したら、 それは あまり 勉強[べんきょう] しなかったと いう ことですよ。
If you did not understand this problem, it means you didn't study very much.

（もし）S としたら Sとしたら literally means "If I/we/you suppose that S." This construction is usually used to present a hypothetical situation, but can be used for an actual situation as well in which the speaker is presenting the situation as if it were hypothetical in order to indicate something indirectly. もし here is optional. It emphasizes that the speaker is presenting the situation as a hypothetical one
スミスさんは、 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]だ。 なぜかと いうと、 日本[にほん]に 長[なが]く 住[す]んでいたからだ。

Sの（だろう／でしょう）か Means: I wonder ~ Indicates a self-addressed question which can either be a yes-no question or a wh- question.

少なくとも Number (+Counter) 少なくとも means "at least." It can be used with a noun or number (optionally followed by a counter). When は follows a number (+counter), it emphasizes the number.

S-plain {ということは／なんて} 考えられない "unimaginable, unthinkable, inconeivable"
かなり ゆっくり 話[はな]してあげたのに、 あの 人[ひと]は 私[わたし]の 言[い]った ことが あまり 分[わ]からなかった ようだ。

どんどん-V "at a fast pace; one after another; keep V-ing vigorously; with no hesitation; with no delay" どんどん expresses the idea that something proceeds from one stage to the next or continues to happen at a fast pace with no delay, or that someone keeps doing something with no hesitation. ~わけだ。 Means: The reason is that~; it means that~; that's why~; no wonder~; naturally Can be used in 3 situations, here it is (2) when a speaker reaches a logical conclusion based on what he/she has learned from the hearer or has discovered.
日食[にっしょく] (solar eclipse)を 見[み]ている うちに、 どんどん 空[そら]が 暗[くら]くなってきて、 ついに 真[ま]っ暗[くら]になってしまった。
As I watched the solar eclipse, the sky got rapidly darker and darker and finally became pitch black.

どんどん-V "at a fast pace; one after another; keep V-ing vigorously; with no hesitation; with no delay" どんどん expresses the idea that something proceeds from one stage to the next or continues to happen at a fast pace with no delay, or that someone keeps doing something with no hesitation. In some situations both ますますand どんどん can be used, bearing in mind that ますます does not convey the idea that something happens at a fast pace and cannot describe a controllable future action.

In 1964 the Summer Olympics were held in Tokyo and in 1998 the Winter Olympics were held in Nagano.

N1 において V "in;at;on;during" The compound particle における indicate the place or time of an action, event, or state. The pre-verbal form is において. Both are used only in formal language.
A: 今度[こんど]の ミーティングは 金曜[きんよう] 日[び]で いいですか。 B: あ、 すみません。 その 日[ひ]は ちょっと、、、。 それ 以外[いがい]の 日[ひ]に していただけませんか。
A: Is Friday fine for our next meeting? B: Oh, I'm sorry, Friday is not good for me. Could we make it another day?

{N1/DemP} 以外の N2 "but; except; other than; besides" X以外のY means "Y, excluding X." のY is often omitted.

cost per person

説明 [explanation]: 当たり is used with ー (or 1) and a counter to mean "per." Sometimes numbers other than one are used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: per~; a ~; for a ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number + Counter 当たり Number + Counter b. Number + Counter 当たりの N

歯[は]が シクシク する。

説明 [explanation]: 当たり is used with ー (or 1) and a counter to mean "per." Sometimes numbers other than one are used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: per~; a ~; for a ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number + Counter 当たり Number + Counter b. Number + Counter 当たりの N

説明 [explanation]: In some situations, A in A の B is a Noun with a particle such as へ, で, と, から, and まで. が, を and に never occur in this position. Note that の cannot be omitted in this case because it indicates that the preceeding noun phrase and particle modifies the following noun phrase. Without の, the noun phrase with the particle is interpreted as an adverbial phrase modifying the predicate in the clause, i.e. compare 先生とミーチングに行けない。(I can't go to meet the teacher) and 先生とのミーチングに行けない。(I can't go to the meeting with the teacher). --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Noun + Particle + の + Noun

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. Note: でしょう and だろう with falling intonation indicate conjecture. --- 英訳 [English translation]: tag question(e.g. isn't it?; wasn't it?; aren't they?; is he?; are they?) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~だろう, ~でしょう
言葉[ことば]は 時代[じだい]と 共[とも]に 変化[へんか] する。

As long as I have love, I am happy.

説明 [explanation]: Noun さえ with a verb conditional form is used when the condition presented in the clause is the only condition to make the statement in the main clause true. さえ replaces が and を in this structure; however, when other particles occur with さえ here, they do not drop. --- 英訳 [English translation]: If~ only ~; If~ just ~; as long as; --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N( = clause X) さえ V-cond (= clause Y)

Here. You can use this dictionary if it'll do.

N でよければ Means: if ~ is all right; if ~ works; if ~ is acceptable; if you don't mind it presents a condition for doing something. it is also used when the speaker politely offers something to the hearer.

説明 [explanation]: {で/から}できる means "to be made of/from/out of." から indicates that the material(s) from which something is made is not immediately obvious. できる is used in generic statements while できている is used when describing something specific. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~でできる = be made of; be made out of ~からできる = be made from --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N {で / から} {できる / できている} --- The difference between raw material and material/ingredient is whether the material undergoes qualitative transformation in the production process. Typically, when there is a qualitative change, から is used; when there is no qualitative change, で is used.
この 電子[でんし] 辞書[じしょ]、 いくらだったっけ？
How much was this electronic dictionary again?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{ANa/N/QW} だった (んだ) っけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。
ちょっと、 その 本[ほん]、 取[と]ってくれない?
Could you grab that book for me?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-te くれる, etc. with rising intonation is used to make request in casual conversation. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Will you ~?; Can you ~?; Could you~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te {くれる / くれない / もらえる / もらえない}
友達[ともだち]同士[どうし]で 話[はな]し合[あ]って 決[き]めて下[くだ]さい。

N同士 {が／で／を} Indicates that Ns do something together, that Ns do something to/for/against each other, or that someone puts Ns together in some way.

Reading is one of my favorite things.

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to describe X while indicating that X is not the only example, object, person, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X is one of the ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ NはNPの{一つ/一人}だ。
私[わたし]の モットーは 「健康[けんこう]が 第[だい]一[いち]」です。
My motto is "health first".
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N が第一 だ。 "first; first of all; to begin with; the first; the primary"
なかなか 面白[おもしろ]い ことに 気[き]が つきました。
I noticed something pretty interesting.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N に気がつく。 Means: notice (that~); realize that ~ Notice that the presence of こと in a sentence using this grammar will not always be the nominalizer meaning "thing." It could be the Sこと form for statements using this grammar.
一[いち]日[にち]当[あ]たり ５千[ごせん]円[えん] もらった ことに なる。
So that means I got 5,000 yen per day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 当たり is used with ー (or 1) and a counter to mean "per." Sometimes numbers other than one are used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: per~; a ~; for a ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number + Counter 当たり Number + Counter b. Number + Counter 当たりの N
日本[にほん]語[ご]の 文法[ぶんぽう]が 面白[おもしろ]くなってきました。
I'm beginning to find Japanese grammar interesting.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-teくる and V-teいく indicate the temporal or spatial direction of an action from the speaker's viewpoint. V-te来る is used when an action appears to be directed toward the speaker, and V-te行く is used when it appears to be directed away from the speaker. V-teくる often indicates that an action or process began in the past and is continuing in the present, or that something has begun to take place. V-teいく, on the other hand, often expresses an action or state that will continue from the present into the future. In other uses, 来る and 行くfollowing V-te maintain their original meanings, i.e., "to come" and "to go." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-teくる = have V-ed; begin to; become; grow V−teいく = go on V-ing; continue; become; grow --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te来る/行く
この 記事[きじ]、 読[よ]むの、 手伝[てつだ]ってくれない？
Won't you help me read this article?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-te くれる, etc. with rising intonation is used to make request in casual conversation. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Will you ~?; Can you ~?; Could you~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te {くれる / くれない / もらえる / もらえない}
あの 話[はなし]は 本当[ほんとう]では ないと 言[い]われています。
It is said that that story is not true.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

〜である/~ではない is the formal plain form of だ and can be affixed to nouns and -な／-の adjectives. である is used in formal writing. In very formal speech the polite form であります／ではありません may be used. である can occur before nouns in relative clauses while だ cannot.
思[おも]わぬ 結果[けっか]に なって、 びっくり している。
I'm surprised to get such an unexpected result.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-nai ぬ "not" ぬ is a verb ending from classical Japanese and is equivalent to ない in meaning and form. In modern Japanese, it often appears in set phrases.
この さむらい風[ふう]の 人形[にんぎょう]は、 いくらですか。
How much does this samurai-style doll cost?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 風の N2 "~style; ~type; look like" 風 is a suffix and is added to nouns to make no-adjectives. X風 means "X style/type" or "looks like X"
この 辺[へん]は、 あまり 安全[あんぜん]じゃない 気[き]が する。
I get the feeling that this area isn't very safe.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

~(ような）気がする Meaning; I feel that~: I have a feeling that ~; have the impression that ~; it seems to me that~ It indicates that the speaker is not certain about something, but has the feeling that it's true. ような can be dropped without changing the meaning.
お星[ほし]さまが キラキラ して、 きれいだなあ。
The stars are twinkling. They are so pretty!
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N が (onomatopoeia) する。 This construction with ono phrases is used to describe one's physiological/phychological state or way something feels or looks.
これほど すばらしい 絵[え]を 見[み]た ことが ない。
I've never seen a picture as great as this.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

DemPほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb
明日[あした]は テストが 無[な]いって 聞[き]いたけど、 本当[ほんとう]？
I heard there isn't a test tomorrow, but is that true?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: って is the informal colloquial form of the quotative marker と. って commonly occurs with verbs like 言う, 聞く, 書く and 呼ぶ. --- 英訳 [English translation]: (tell, hear, say, etc.) that ~ Noun1っていうNoun2 = Noun2 called Noun1 --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Sって{言う/聞く/書く} b. Nって{言う/聞く/呼ぶ} c. N1っていうN2
ドラえもんは 実[じつ]は ネコ型[がた] ロボットなんです。
Doraemon is, in reality, a cat-shaped robot.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 型 is a suffix meaning "style, type, model, etc." It is commonly used to describe the shape, type, model, or newness of an object. The preceding elements are mostly nouns, but some adjectival kanji characters can also precede 型(e.g. 大, 新, 薄). --- 英訳 [English translation]: style; type; pattern; make; model; design --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 型だ b. N1 + 型(の)N2
両親[りょうしん]は、 元気[げんき]な うちに 旅行[りょこう] する ことに した。
My parents have decided to take a trip while they're still feeling up to it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (ない)うちに is used when someone does something before a situation or state changes. 間に is used in similar situations, but it cannot be used with the negative forms of verbs. Another difference between the two phrases is that うちに always implies that it is not possible, easy or a good idea to do something after the time specified by the うちに clause. However, this is not always the case with 間に. Thus far, if it is not a problem for the speaker to go to Japan after finishing his Japanese class, 間に should be used, as shown below: 日本語の勉強をしている間に日本に行ってみたい。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: while ~ still ～ないうちに＝ before (something happens) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ～うちに
新[あたら]しい 車[くるま]を 買[か]う ために お金[かね]を 貯[た]めています。
I am saving up money so that I can buy a new car.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) This construction is used to state either a purpose or the way in which something is to be done. In XようにY, X represents a state or event which is beyond the control of the subject of Y. The verb form before ように is often a potential form or a negative form. (2) In the similar construction XためにY, X represents an action which can be controlled by the subject of Y, while XようにY implies that a certain consequence (X) will arise as the result of an action (Y). --- 英訳 [English translation]: so that ~; in such a way that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastように
先生[せんせい]、 この 文法[ぶんぽう] よく 分[わ]からないんですが。。。
Teacher, I don't understand this grammar very well, so... (could you help me with it?)
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: S んだけど／ですが is used as a preliminary remark by the speaker to inform the hearer of the speaker's desire, the current situation, etc. before (a) asking a question related to that desire, (b) asking for an opinion on the matter, or (c) making a request. This phrase can also be used to extend an invitation or an offer. When making a request, the request is often unstated, as shown below. んだけど is more casual than んですが. --- 英訳 [English translation]: but (in english, null in most situations) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜ん{だけど/ですが}
早[はや]く 辞書[じしょ] なしで 新聞[しんぶん]が 読[よ]める ようになりたい。
I want to be able to read a newspaper without a dictionary soon.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N なし で V "without ~; with no ~"
運動[うんどう]は 体[からだ]に いい。 その 上[うえ]、 心[こころ]の 健康[けんこう]にも いい。
Exercise is good for the body. On top of that, it's also good for your mental health.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1. その上、S2. Means: on top of that; in addition (to that); what's more; besides; moreover その上 is used when the speaker wants to emphasize an additional piece of information. S2 usually contains the particle も or まで。 as here.
先生[せんせい]は 学生[がくせい]に 漢字[かんじ]を 覚[おぼ]える ように 言[い]いました。
The teacher told the students to remember the kanji.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
一[いっ]週間[しゅうかん]に 一[いっ]回[かい]は プールで 泳[およ]ぐ ようにしている。
I'm trying to swim at the pool at least once a week.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When the particle は follows a quantifier (i.e., a word such as 3本 or 少し), it adds the meaning "at least." だけは and ぐらいは (or くらいは) after a noun have the same meaning. --- 英訳 [English translation]: at least. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) は b. N だけは c. N {ぐらい/くらい}は
これから 公園[こうえん]へ サッカーを しに 行[い]く ところです。
I'm just about to go to the park to play soccer.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-nonpast ところ Means: (when) ~is about to V
日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]になる ように、 毎日[まいにち] 練習[れんしゅう] している。
I practice every day so that I'll become good at Japanese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) This construction is used to state either a purpose or the way in which something is to be done. In XようにY, X represents a state or event which is beyond the control of the subject of Y. The verb form before ように is often a potential form or a negative form. (2) In the similar construction XためにY, X represents an action which can be controlled by the subject of Y, while XようにY implies that a certain consequence (X) will arise as the result of an action (Y). --- 英訳 [English translation]: so that ~; in such a way that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastように
山田[やまだ]さん、 できたら 果物[くだもの]を 持[も]って来[き]てくれない？
Mr. Yamada, if possible, could you bring fruits with you for me?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The phrase literally means "if possible." It is also used when the speaker asks a favor of someone in a less direct way. できれば is slightly more formal than できたら. --- 英訳 [English translation]: if possible; if you don't mind; if it's all right --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ できれば／できたら
暑[あつ]いのは 好[す]きでは ないが、 寒[さむ]いのも また 苦手[にがて]だ。
I don't like hot weather, but I'm not a fan of cold weather, either.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
もまた "as well; also; too" In this usage もまた means the same as も; however it is more emphatic and formal than も.
空[そら]の 様子[ようす]から すると、 夕方[ゆうがた]には 雨[あめ]に なる ようだ。
Judging from how the sky looks, it seems it'll rain this evening.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nからすると "judging from~" Introduces the source or basis for the speaker's conjecture or judgment. The information can be of any sort including visual or verbal.
日本[にほん]には、 本州[ほんしゅう]を はじめ 四[よっ]つの 大[おお]きな 島[しま]が ある。
Japan, starting with Honshuu, has four large islands.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun をはじめ is used to present a primary example when mentioning a group of things or people. --- 英訳 [English translation]: beginning with~; starting with ~; including ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをはじめ
辞書[じしょ]を 見[み]ずに 新聞[しんぶん]が 読[よ]める ようになりたいです。
I would like to become able to read a newspaper without looking at the dictionary.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ずに is synonymous with ないで when ないで means "without doing something" or "instead of doing something." に is sometimes omitted. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Without V-ing; instead of V-ing --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-naiずに: 行かずに; 食べずに (Exception: する->せずに
毎日[まいにち]、 新[あたら]しい 漢字[かんじ]を 五つ[いつつ] 覚[おぼ]える ことに している。

Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Indicates THE SPEAKER (or the subject of the sentence) makes it a rule to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: make it a rule that; I decided that --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastことにしている
私[わたし]は 毎日[まいにち] 漢字[かんじ]を 五つ[いつつ]ずつ 覚[おぼ]える ことに している。
I make it a rule to memorize five kanji a day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{Number +(counter)} +ずつ "per/a; at a time; each; (little) by (little)" The number/amount X+ずつ indicates that someone does something (or something happens) with X as the unit.
サービスと いう 点[てん]では、 日本[にほん]の デパートは 最高[さいこう]だ。
Japanese department stores are the best in terms of service.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N {という/の} 点で (は） "in terms of ~; with regard to ~; with respect to ~" 点 is used to mean "point" (in the sense of a single, fact, idea or opinion in an argument, discussion, etc.), "aspect," or "viewpoint/standpoint."
ステーキに サラダ、 それに ライスも お願[ねが]いします。
I'd like a steak, a salad and some rice as well, please.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: それに is used to add an item or make an addition statement. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in addition; moreover; furthermore; what's more; on top of that; and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {、/と / に} N2, それに N3 b. S1。それに、S2。 c. S1 し、それに、S2。
今[いま]は もう コンピュータ なしの 生活[せいかつ]は 考[かんが]えられない。
I can't even imagine life without computers now.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N なし の N "without ~; with no ~"
レストラン、 予約[よやく] しといたからさ、 7[しち]時[じ]に 来[き]てね。
I reserved a table at the restaurant, so be there at 7, OK?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

phrase/clause/sentence さ(あ) "(you know)" さ occurs after phrases, clauses, or sentences in very casual conversation. One function is to catch the hearer's attention, but it is also used as a filler with no meaning.
車[くるま]を 運転[うんてん] するのなら、 お酒[さけ]を 飲[の]んでは いけません。
If you're going to drive, you can't drink.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: なら is used when the speaker supposes that something is the case or is true and makes a statement, suggestion, etc. based on that supposition. の occurs before なら when the supposition is based on what the speaker has heard from someone or learned from the situation. Nなら means "if it is N; N would/could ~." In "S1 なら S2", the action/event in S1 does not have to take place before that in S2. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Nなら = would; could~ S(の)なら = if (it's the case that) ~; if (it's true that) ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~(の)なら
この ホテルは 静[しず]かな 上[うえ]に、 サービスが とても いい。
This hotel's not just quiet, it also has excellent service.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S 上に "in addition to~; besides~; not only~but also~; moreover~; ~ as well" The conjunction 上に introduces additional information emphatically.
私[わたし]に とって 何[なに]よりも 大切[たいせつ]なのは、 家族[かぞく]の 幸[しあわ]せです。
What's more important to me than anything else is my family's happiness.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
何より（も） "before everything; above all; first of all; more than anything else; the most ~"
私[わたし]は よく 両親[りょうしん]に 弟[おとうと]を いじめない ように 言[い]われます。
I'm often told by my parents not to tease my little brother.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
その トピックに 関係[かんけい]の ある 本[ほん]は この 列[れつ]に あります。

N1 {と/に} 関係 {が/の} あるN2. This sentence is used to show that N1 is related in someway to N2. The particle after N1 may be と or に。 When this pattern is used in relative clauses, の is commonly used after 関係 instead of が。

Fortunately, even though I've gotten older, at least my body is healthy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANa なことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.
先生[せんせい]は 学生[がくせい]に 「漢字[かんじ]を 覚[おぼ]えなさい」と 言[い]いました。
The teacher said to the students, "Remember the kanji."

(cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
漢字[かんじ]は 日本[にほん]語[ご]の 勉強[べんきょう]で 最[もっと]も 大切[たいせつ]な ものの 一[ひと]つです。
Kanji is one of the most important things in the study of Japanese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to describe X while indicating that X is not the only example, object, person, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X is one of the ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ NはNPの{一つ/一人}だ。
それらの 点[てん]に ついて もう 一度[いちど] 調[しら]べてみる つもりです。
I intend to try looking into those points again.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Personal pronoun ら "these; those; they; -s; and others" [plural dem. pronouns can be used in polite speech] The plural marker ら is often used with demonstrative pronouns and certain personal pronouns. plural personal pronouns are not used in polite speech.
私[わたし]が 取[と]っているのは、 中国[ちゅうごく]語[ご]では なくて 日本[にほん]語[ご]です。
What I'm taking is Japanese, not Chinese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that a certain piece of information is wrong and, following that, to present the correct information. ではなく(て) is used in written language and じゃなく(て) is used in spoken language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: not A, but B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {では/じゃ}なく(て) N2 b. Phrase1 {では/じゃ}なく(て) Phrase2
どんなに 大変[たいへん]でも、 日本[にほん]語[ご]の 勉強[べんきょう]は 決[けっ]して やめない。
No matter how hard it gets, there's no way I'll give up studying Japanese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

決してV-nai { ない／なかった} 決して V-masu {ません／ませんでした} "Never; by no means; not~ at all; not ~ in the least; definitely not" expresses strong negation of an idea, situation, possibility, etc. or strong prohibition
せっかくの 野球[やきゅう]の 試合[しあい]が 雨[あめ]で 中止[ちゅうし]に なってしまった。
The baseball game we'd been looking forward to ended up being called off due to rain.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

せっかくのN "with effort; at great pain; take the trouble to do ~; ~, which is a rare occasion/event/etc." せっかく is used in 2 situations: (2) when a given opportunity is rare and therefore he/she wants to make use of it; or, in spite of their opportunity, he/she cannot make use of it
今[いま] 勉強[べんきょう]中[ちゅう]だから、 もう ちょっと 静[しず]かにしてもらえる？
I'm in the middle of studying right now, so could you be a little more quiet?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-te くれる, etc. with rising intonation is used to make request in casual conversation. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Will you ~?; Can you ~?; Could you~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te {くれる / くれない / もらえる / もらえない}
今日[きょう]の 試験[しけん]の ほとんどの 問題[もんだい]が、 宿題[しゅくだい]と 同[おな]じだった。
Most of the questions on the test today were the same as the ones from the homework.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほとんどの N means Almost all N; most of N
年末[ねんまつ]から 年始[ねんし]に かけて、 ヨーロッパを 旅行[りょこう] しました。
I traveled in Europe from year end into the new year.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 から N2 にかけて "from N1 to N2" indicates a span of time or space and is used primarily in written language.
両親[りょうしん]に 相談[そうだん] せずに、 入学[にゅうがく] する ことを 決[き]めてしまった。

Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ずに is synonymous with ないで when ないで means "without doing something" or "instead of doing something." に is sometimes omitted. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Without V-ing; instead of V-ing --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-naiずに: 行かずに; 食べずに (Exception: する->せずに
この 絵本[えほん]は 読[よ]んで 面白[おもしろ]いと 同時[どうじ]に、 考[かんが]えさせられる。
This picture book is an enjoyable read, and, at the same time, it makes you think.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{V/A}-plain.non-pastと同時に "as soon as; the moment; at the same time; also; as well"
田中[たなか]さんは、 健康[けんこう]上[じょう]の 問題[もんだい]が あって、 仕事[しごと]を 辞[や]めた。
Tanaka resigned due to health problems.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 上の N2 "in terms of; from the viewpoint of ~; as far as ~ is concerned; according to ~" Nの上で and N上 are used to indicate that the speaker's statement refers only to N. Commonly used in written language.
この 植木[うえき]は ２[に]週間[しゅうかん]に 一度[いちど] 水[みず]を やるだけで いいですよ。
All you have to do for this plant is water it once every two weeks.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V-plain.non-past/N} だけで {いい／十分だ／etc.} "just with ~; just by V-ing (is fine/enough/etc.) N/Vだけで is used to express the idea that X or just doing X is fine or good enough or that one can do something just with X or by doing X.
漢字[かんじ]の 勉強[べんきょう]は 覚[おぼ]え方[かた] 次第[しだい]で 大変[たいへん]じゃなくなりますよ。
Studying kanji doesn't have to be hard, depending on how you memorize the characters.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N次第で "depending on N" When 次第 is affixed to nouns, it means "depend on."
その 店[みせ]が 美味[おい]しかったか まずかったか 覚[おぼ]えていますか。
Do you remember whether (the food at) that store was delicious or bad?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The phrase AかBか is used to present alternatives. When Bか is followed by a case particle (e.g., が, を, へ, に, で, と), the second か is usually dropped. --- 英訳 [English translation]: either A or B; whether A or B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. 〜か〜か b. N1かN2+Particle
多[おお]くの 人々[ひとびと]が 早[はや]く 世界[せかい]が 平和[へいわ]になる ように願[ねが]っている。
Many people hope that we'll have a peaceful world soon.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain.nonpast ように（と）願う Means: hope that ~ And is used to express the speaker's hope or desire that what is stated in the sentence will become a reality.
友達[ともだち]が 手伝[てつだ]ってくれた おかげで、 仕事[しごと]が 早[はや]く終[お]わった。
Thanks to my friend helping me out, work ended early.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain おかげ "because; due to" Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result.
海外[かいがい] 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]く 前[まえ]に パスポートを 取[と]る 必要[ひつよう]が あります。
Before traveling overseas it is necessary to get a passport.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This phrase is used to indicate the necessity of doing something. は is common with a negative ending. --- 英訳 [English translation]: a. V必要がある = It is necessary to V; must V; have to V. b. V必要はない = It is not necessary to V; there is no need to V; don't have to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past 必要{がある/はない}
今年[ことし]の 夏[なつ]は 寒[さむ]い 日[ひ]が 続[つづ]いて、 全然[ぜんぜん] 夏[なつ]らしく ありません。
Summer this year has been cold day after day; it doesn't feel summery at all.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜らしくない／らしくありません Means: not much like, not typical of ~; not typical~; not X-like.
人生[じんせい]は 考[かんが]え方[かた] 次第[しだい]で、 楽[たの]しくも なれば、 苦[くる]しくも なる。
Your life can be enjoyable or painful depending on how you view things.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

A-stem くも V-cond ば, 〜も "some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well" This structure is used to present actions or states (usually 2) as examples of possible or past actions/states. In many cases the actions/states are contrastive ones.
あ、 ちょっと、 静[しず]かにして！ ほら、 鳥[とり]の 声[こえ]が 聞[き]こえる！
Be quiet for a sec! Listen - I hear birds chirping!
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほら "Look!; See?; Come on!" The interjection ほら can be used to draw the hearer's attention to something. Only used in very casual conversation.
この 教科[きょうか]書[しょ]は、 会話[かいわ]も 練習[れんしゅう] できるし、 文化[ぶんか]も 学[まな]べます。
With this textbook you can practice conversation and study culture among other things.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1も V-plain し、N2も V Means: do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well; other meanings exist: pg 142 in とびら
この 教科[きょうか]書[しょ]は、 会話[かいわ]も 練習[れんしゅう] できれば、 文化[ぶんか]も 学[まな]べます。
With this textbook you can practice conversation and study culture among other things.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1も V-conditional, N2 も V。 Means: some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well. This sentence structure is used to present some members in a group, things in a category, actions someone takes, characteristics of something/someone, etc. among others. Although the form of the verb here is conditional, the meaning is NOT conditional in its usage.
数学[すうがく]と 同[おな]じで、 物理[ぶつり]も 公式[こうしき]を 勉強[べんきょう] しなくては ならない。
You have to study formulas when you study physics, just like when you study math.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The comparison phrases と同じで and と違って mean "just like ~" and "unlike ~", respectively. Note that the particle と is used when X and Y are in a reciprocal relationship --- 英訳 [English translation]: N と同じで = just like N N と違って = unlike N; different from N --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N と{同じ/違って}
新型[しんがた]の インフルエンザの ワクチンは、 まだ ない そうだ。
I heard they don't have a vaccine for the new strain of influenza yet.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 型 is a suffix meaning "style, type, model, etc." It is commonly used to describe the shape, type, model, or newness of an object. The preceding elements are mostly nouns, but some adjectival kanji characters can also precede 型(e.g. 大, 新, 薄). --- 英訳 [English translation]: style; type; pattern; make; model; design --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 型だ b. N1 + 型(の)N2
父[ちち]は 病気[びょうき]に なってから、 お酒[さけ]を 飲[の]まない ようになった。
Since my father became ill, he no longer drinks sake.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ようになる indicates a gradual change over a certain period of time; it means that someone (or something) comes to the point where he/she does (or can do) something or does not (or cannot) do something. V-なくなる is synonymous with V-ないようになる. The difference is that the latter implies a more gradual change. --- 英訳 [English translation]: come to (be able to) V; not V now; not V any more. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようになる (V is often the potential form)
便利[べんり]さと いう 点[てん]から 考[かんが]えると、 この アパートが 一番[いちばん]だ。
From a convenience standpoint, this apartment is the best.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N という点から考えると "to view from the standpoint of ~; from the perspective of ~" used to indicate someone's view from the standpoint of X. Examples of X include business, environment, education, etc.
暑[あつ]くならない うちに、 犬[いぬ]の 散歩[さんぽ]を してきた 方[ほう]が いいよ。
It's best to walk the dog before it becomes hot outside.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (ない)うちに is used when someone does something before a situation or state changes. 間に is used in similar situations, but it cannot be used with the negative forms of verbs. Another difference between the two phrases is that うちに always implies that it is not possible, easy or a good idea to do something after the time specified by the うちに clause. However, this is not always the case with 間に. Thus far, if it is not a problem for the speaker to go to Japan after finishing his Japanese class, 間に should be used, as shown below: 日本語の勉強をしている間に日本に行ってみたい。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: while ~ still ～ないうちに＝ before (something happens) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ～うちに
ゾウは 長[なが]い 鼻[はな]を しています。 それに、 耳[みみ]も 大[おお]きいです。
Elephants have long noses. Furthermore, they have big ears.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This pattern is used to describe a feature of someone or something, focusing on a certain part or attribute of the person or thing. -- When the phrase modifies a noun, した is commonly used instead of している. Synonyous with N1はN2がAdj. --- 英訳 [English translation]: have --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 は Adj+N2 をしている b. Adj+N2 をした N1
この 漢字[かんじ]の 書[か]き方[かた]は、 覚[おぼ]えても 覚[おぼ]えなくても いいです。
It doesn't matter whether or not you memorize the way to write this kanji.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-te も V-nai なくても "Whether V or not"
漢字[かんじ]が 苦手[にがて]だと 言[い]っても、 全然[ぜんぜん] 書[か]けない わけでは ない。
Although I say that kanji is my weak point, that doesn't mean I can't write them at all.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{V/A} (という）わけではない。 Means: It's not that~; It doesn't mean that used to deny a statement.
この アパート、 良[よ]さ そうだけど、 ちょっと 高[たか]すぎるかな。
This apartment seems nice, but I wonder if it's a bit too expensive.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 〜かなあ is a sentence final particle which indicates that the sentence is a self-addressed question or a question addressed to the speaker's in-group member(s). It is used only in casual language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I wonder ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜かな(あ)
YouTubeは 面白[おもしろ]い。だが、 問題[もんだい]の ある 動画[どうが]も 多[おお]い。
YouTube is interesting, but there are also a lot of problematic video clips.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1. だが、S2. "but; however" だが is a disjunctive conjunction. S1 and S2 present contrastive statements or opposing ideas. Note: でも、けれど、けど are colloquial けれども、しかしながら、だが、and が are primarily used in written language. しかし can be used in both written and spoken language.
これらの 問題[もんだい]に ついて もっと 話[はな]し合[あ]ってみる 必要[ひつよう]が ある。
We need to try discussing these problems more.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Demonstrative pronounら "these; those; they; -s; and others" [plural dem. pronouns can be used in polite speech] The plural marker ら is often used with demonstrative pronouns and certain personal pronouns. plural personal pronouns are not used in polite speech.
明日[あした]の 試験[しけん]では、 言[い]うまでも なく、 文法[ぶんぽう]の 問題[もんだい]が 出[で]ます。
Needless to say, there will be grammar questions on tomorrow's test.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

（Xは）言うまでもなく、S。 "needless to say; it goes without saying that ~; it is obvious that ~; not to mention ~; let alone ~" This phrase is used when the speaker mentions something obvious or something assumed to be known to the hearer. It is commonly used in written language.
今度[こんど] 住[す]む アパートは、 この 部屋[へや]と 同[おな]じぐらいの 広[ひろ]さです。
The apartment I'm going to live in next is about the same size as this room.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The particle ぐらい/くらい "approximately" often occurs with 同じ to mean "about the same." --- 英訳 [English translation]: about as ~ as; about the same ~ as ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N と同じ{ぐらい/くらい} b. N1 と同じ{ぐらい/くらい}の N2
母[はは]の 料理[りょうり]が いかに おいしいかは、 言葉[ことば]では 説明[せつめい] できない。
There are no words to describe just how delicious my mother's cooking is.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
いかに〜か "how; how much; in what way" This structure occurs as an embedded interrogative sentence, where いかに means "how (much)" or "in what way". This structure is commonly used in written language.
田中[たなか]さん、 ５[ご]時[じ]に 来[く]るって 言[い]ってたけど、 未[いま]だ 来[こ]ないね。
Mr. Tanaka said he'd come at 5:00, but he still hasn't come, has he?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: って is the informal colloquial form of the quotative marker と. って commonly occurs with verbs like 言う, 聞く, 書く and 呼ぶ. --- 英訳 [English translation]: (tell, hear, say, etc.) that ~ Noun1っていうNoun2 = Noun2 called Noun1 --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Sって{言う/聞く/書く} b. Nって{言う/聞く/呼ぶ} c. N1っていうN2
両親[りょうしん]は 私[わたし]に、 いつも 早[はや]く 家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]ってくる ように 言[い]います。
My parents always tell me to come home early.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
漢字[かんじ]を 覚[おぼ]えるには フラッシュ カードを 作[つく]るのが 一番[いちばん]です。
Making flash cards is the best way to memorize kanji.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past.aff には "to; in order to; for; for the purpose of; when" には indicates purpose in general statements (often stating the speaker's judgement about an action in terms of its effectiveness, convenience, necessity, etc.). には can also mean "when" (=時には). Verbs or nouns can precede には. Note that when ために is used, the predicate in the main clause describes an action. Such that: Xには Y, where Y is a judgment and never an action XためにY, where Y is an action and never a judgement. AND, XためにはY, where Y is a judgment, never an action
大学[だいがく]に 入[はい]って 以来[いらい]、 高校[こうこう] 時代[じだい]の 友達[ともだち]に 一度[いちど]も 会[あ]っていない。
I haven't seen my high school friends even once since I started college.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-te 以来 "since" It is used with V-te or VN referring to an action in the past, or with N indicating a specific time in the past.
ハンサムな せいで、 うそを 信[しん]じて、 ばかな ことを しました。
Because he was handsome, I believed his lies and did foolish things.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANa {な/じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} せい／おかげ "because; due to" Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result. Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result.
宿題[しゅくだい]を しようと したが、 友達[ともだち]が 来[き]たから、 するのを やめた。
I was going to do my homework, but friends came over so I stopped doing it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-volとした, the past form of V-volとする(to try to do ~), is used in situations when someone had made an attempt to do something but failed, where someone was going to do something but didn't, or where something happened when someone was going to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-volとした{が／けれど} = tried to ~, but; was going to ~, but V-volとしたら = when ~ was going to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-volとした{が／けれど}: 行こうとした{が／けれど／ら}; 食べようとした{が／けれど／ら}
私[わたし]は 来週[らいしゅう]、 学校[がっこう]の 代表[だいひょう]と して スピーチ コンテストに 出[で]ます。
Next week, I'm participating in a speech contest as the representative from my school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: として is used to indicate the role, capacity, or occupation of someone or the function or characteristics of something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: as; in the capacity of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nとして1
お酒[さけ]さえ 飲[の]まなければ、 何[なに]を 飲[の]んでも 食[た]べても いいですよ。
You can drink and eat whatever you want as long as you don't drink alcohol.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun さえ with a verb conditional form is used when the condition presented in the clause is the only condition to make the statement in the main clause true. さえ replaces が and を in this structure; however, when other particles occur with さえ here, they do not drop. --- 英訳 [English translation]: If~ only ~; If~ just ~; as long as; --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N( = clause X) さえ V-cond (= clause Y)
週末[しゅうまつ]は、 勉強[べんきょう] 以外[いがい]に、 テニスを したり 映画[えいが]を 見[み]たり します。
Besides studying, I do things like play tennis and watch movies on the weekend.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{N/DemP} 以外に "Besides N/DemP" X以外に means "besides X" and に is sometimes omitted.
人々[ひとびと]の 生活[せいかつ]の 変化[へんか]に 合[あ]わせて、 家[いえ]の 形[かたち]も 変[か]わってきました。
Housing styles have also changed to match the change in people's lifestyles.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N に会わせて "making ~ suitable for N; according to N" The literal meaning this grammar is "fitting/matching/adjusting something to N" and is often used to mean "making something suitable for N" or "according to N"
調[しら]べなきゃならない ことが あるので、 図書[としょ]館[かん]に 行[い]って来[く]る。
I have things I have to research so I'm going to the library.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). The following contracted forms are used in casual conversation: なきゃならない -> なきゃなんない なくちゃならない -> なくちゃんなんない --- 英訳 [English translation]: have to; must; should --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜なければ{いけない/ならない} 〜なくては{いけない/ならない}
みんなが 同時[どうじ]に 話[はな]さないで、 一人[ひとり]ずつ 順番[じゅんばん]に 話[はな]して下[くだ]さい。
Please don't all talk at once - take turns and speak one at a time.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{Number +(counter)} +ずつ "per/a; at a time; each; (little) by (little)" The number/amount X+ずつ indicates that someone does something (or something happens) with X as the unit.
分[わ]からない ときは、 もう 一度[いちど]、 読[よ]み直[なお]してみるといいですよ。
When you don't understand something, it helps to try reading it one more time.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-masu 直す "again, re-V" 直す, when attached to the masu-stems of verbs, creates compound verbs with the meaning "again; re-."
残念[ざんねん]な ことに、 私[わたし]達[たち]の チームは 最後[さいご]の 試合[しあい]で 負[ま]けてしまった。
Unfortunately, our team lost in the last match.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANa なことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.
私[わたし]の 国[くに]では 日本[にほん]に 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]く 時[とき]、 旅行[りょこう] ビザを 取[と]る 必要[ひつよう]は ない。
As for my country, when traveling to Japan it is not necessary to get a travel Visa.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This phrase is used to indicate the necessity of doing something. は is common with a negative ending. --- 英訳 [English translation]: a. V必要がある = It is necessary to V; must V; have to V. b. V必要はない = It is not necessary to V; there is no need to V; don't have to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past 必要{がある/はない}
日本[にほん]の 有名[ゆうめい]な 小説[しょうせつ]が ハリウッドで 映画[えいが]化[か] される ことに なった。
It's been decided that a famous Japanese novel will be adapted for the screen in Hollywood.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix 化[か] is affixed to nouns and no-adjectives and adds the meaning of "-ization," as in "mechanization" and "digitization." --- 英訳 [English translation]: ～化する = ize; make; become; change to ～化する = ization; making ~; becoming ~; changing to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 化: 日本化; 専門化; 機械化 (mechanization); カタカナ化 b. NO-Adj + 化: 最適化 (optimization)
体[からだ]に いいから、 野菜[やさい]や 果物[くだもの]を たくさん 食[た]べる ようにしている。
Since they're good for you, I'm making an effort to eat lots of vegetables and fruit.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-pastようにする: indicates one's conscious effort to do something for some purpose. Here one makes an effort at every opportunity to do something to the degree that he or she can, but sometimes fails. Thus ようにする is often used for habitual actions. Note that this phrase differs from Vことにする, which indicates one's decision to do something and the action can be either a single or habitual one. --- 英訳 [English translation]: make an effort to~; make an effort so that~; try (one's best) to do ~; try one's best so that~. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようにする: {食べる/食べない}ようにする
その アルバイトは あまり 大変[たいへん]じゃないし、 それに 給料[きゅうりょう]も いい。
That part-time job isn't very difficult, and moreover, the salary is good.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: それに is used to add an item or make an addition statement. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in addition; moreover; furthermore; what's more; on top of that; and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {、/と / に} N2, それに N3 b. S1。それに、S2。 c. S1 し、それに、S2。
インスタント ラーメンは、 たった 3[さん]分[ぷん]で できるので 便利[べんり]です。
Instant ramen takes just three minutes to make, so it's really convenient.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
たった（の）Number (+counter) "only" This is used to emphasize the small amount or number of something.
海外[かいがい] 旅行[りょこう]には、 この スーツケースを 持[も]って行[い]くと 便利[べんり]ですよ。
For traveling overseas, it's useful to take this suitcase with you.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (of a VN, or direct object of する) には "to; in order to; for; for the purpose of; when" には indicates purpose in general statements (often stating the speaker's judgement about an action in terms of its effectiveness, convenience, necessity, etc.). には can also mean "when" (=時には). Verbs or nouns can precede には. Note that when ために is used, the predicate in the main clause describes an action. Such that: Xには Y, where Y is a judgment and never an action XためにY, where Y is an action and never a judgement. AND, XためにはY, where Y is a judgment, never an action
